risk_reasons: Edge security at the request boundary: the CORS block runs FIRST inside proxy(), before isProtectedRoute, so a defect there changes the refusal behaviour of every /api/admin/** request before any auth work happens.
The Admin origin allowlist is the control that replaces 'no CORS exists on this app' as the reason ADR 0025 D7's bearer-wins precedence is not a CSRF hole; a wildcard or over-broad entry reopens it.

The implicit self-origin allowance is load-bearing for the Legacy admin portal: without it every legacy admin POST/PUT/PATCH 403s in production, because a same-origin mutation carries an Origin header (MDN).
src/proxy.ts is shared with #1183 (landed), #1185, #1190, #1192 and #1203; a structural mistake here propagates into four later tickets.
goal: An origin on the Admin origin allowlist can call the Admin API cross-origin — its OPTIONS preflight is answered 204 with the fixed header set before any Supabase work and its real request carries the echoed Access-Control-Allow-Origin — while any other Origin is refused 403 {"error":"origin"} on every method, and every /api/admin/** response carries Vary: Origin.
non_goals: No change to src/proxy.ts branch 4's cookie/bearer authorization behaviour — a bearer still 401s there until #1185; this ticket only adds the CORS block ahead of it and stamps Vary/ACAO on its responses.
No next.config.mjs change: the static headers() block and the global Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin stay byte-for-byte (ADR 0026 D6).
No per-route withAdminCors() wrapper and no OPTIONS handler under src/app/api/admin/** (ADR 0026 D1 rejected both).
No Vercel preview-domain pattern in the allowlist — a pattern is the one thing ADR 0026 D2 forbids.
No WAF rule and no change to docs/runbooks/vercel-waf-rate-limiting.md; the OPTIONS volumetric LOG rule is already live under #1187.
No Access-Control-Allow-Credentials and no Access-Control-Expose-Headers (ADR 0026 D5; no admin route sets a custom response header).
No DELETE in Access-Control-Allow-Methods — no admin route exports DELETE, and adding one later is a deliberate edit here.
No widening of withSameOrigin / assertSameOrigin semantics: assertSameOrigin keeps its four refusal messages and its throw-on-unset-NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL contract.
No impersonation code touched. No migration, no feature flag, no new dependency, no production env write.
No CORS for any path outside /api/admin/**.
user_visible_behavior: OPTIONS /api/admin/<any> with Origin on the Admin origin allowlist → 204, no body, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <the exact echoed origin>, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS, Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, Access-Control-Max-Age: 600, Vary: Origin — and createServerClient is never constructed.
OPTIONS /api/admin/<any> with an Origin that is on no list → 403 {"error":"origin"} with Vary: Origin, no Access-Control-* header of any kind, and no Supabase work.
Any method on /api/admin/** with a refused Origin → 403 {"error":"origin"} before isProtectedRoute and before any Supabase call.

Any method on /api/admin/** with an allowed Origin → the request proceeds to the existing branches, and whatever response comes back carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <the echoed origin> and Vary: Origin — including branch 4's 401/403 refusals.
A request to /api/admin/** with NO Origin header is not origin-checked at all: it reaches the existing auth branch exactly as before (a cookie-less GET still 401s). It still carries Vary: Origin.
A Legacy admin portal same-origin POST/PUT/PATCH (Origin = this app's own origin) is allowed by the implicit self-origin rule and behaves exactly as it does today.
http://localhost:<any port> and http://127.0.0.1:<any port> are admitted outside the production lane (local dev, preview, staging) and refused inside it.
An ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS entry containing '*' makes every /api/admin/** request fail loudly rather than admitting a wildcard origin.
Operationally: ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS is a new server-only Vercel variable with one value per environment; it has no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion and appears in both registries.
invariants: Invariant #1: src/proxy.ts stays Edge-safe — no openai/@anthropic-ai/sdk/bullmq/postgres import, no DB, no node: builtin, in the CORS block or anything it imports.
Invariant #13: ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS is server-authoritative with no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion; ci:static-policy's NEXT_PUBLIC allowlist gains no entry.
ADR 0026 D1: src/proxy.ts is the ONLY place in the repo that writes an Access-Control-* header, and the CORS block is the first thing inside proxy(), ahead of isProtectedRoute.
ADR 0026 D2: no allowlist entry is a pattern — an entry containing '*' throws at read, which is what keeps ADR 0026 D7 true.

ADR 0026 D3: the preflight contract is byte-for-byte — 204 vs 403 {"error":"origin"}, fixed Allow-Methods/Allow-Headers/Max-Age constants never echoed from the request, Vary: Origin on every /api/admin/** response including refusals.
ADR 0026 D4: the origin check applies to every method; this app's own origin is implicitly allowed; a request with no Origin header is untouched by the check.
ADR 0026 D5: no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is ever sent.
One predicate owns 'is this our own origin' and both src/proxy.ts and src/lib/shared/csrf.ts use it — the same single-owner rule Admin transport states for the bearer predicate.
src/lib/config/ stays the sanctioned process.env home (ci:process-env ALLOWLIST_PREFIXES); no new process.env read lands outside it or outside src/proxy.ts, which is off that scan surface.
Invariant #12: the origin DECISION (parse + predicates) lives in a named module with focused tests; only the header WRITING stays inline in the entry point.
edge_cases: Production-lane signal: requiresProductionConfig() (src/lib/config/deployment-lane.ts) is the WRONG predicate here — Vercel sets NODE_ENV=production on staging and preview builds too, so it would make the loopback rule inert on staging, the exact environment ADR 0024 D7 built it for. The lane test is VERCEL_TARGET_ENV === 'production', added as isProductionEnvironment() to src/lib/config/flags.ts, which already declares itself the one home for target-env resolution (isPreviewEnvironment).

Vary: Origin on non-preflight responses: a /api/admin/** request leaves proxy() from four sites today (branch 4's 401, its 403 Forbidden, its 403 mfa_*, and the final pass-through response), and #1185/#1190 add more. Stamping four call sites is fragile, so the existing proxy() body is extracted verbatim into an inner function and the exported proxy() post-stamps the CORS headers on whatever it returns. Branch 4's authorization logic is not touched.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin belongs on the ACTUAL response, not only the preflight: without it a browser blocks every real cross-origin call even after a successful preflight. ADR 0026 D3's table is titled 'the preflight response' but the ticket's first two owed tests are unqualified. Allow-Methods / Allow-Headers / Max-Age stay preflight-only, per spec.

Vary: Origin is set even when the request carried NO Origin header. 'Every /api/admin/** response' is the ADR's word, and the omitted case is exactly the cache-poisoning one it names (a no-Origin response served to an Origin request). 'No Origin means no check' governs the 403, not the header.

Path match: the CORS block matches routePath === '/api/admin' || routePath.startsWith('/api/admin/'), the same set isProtectedRoute uses, not branch 4's looser startsWith('/api/admin'). /api/adminfoo therefore gets no Access-Control-* header; branch 4's own matching is left unchanged (that is #1185's file).

Origin matching is case- and format-normalized through new URL(x).origin on BOTH sides, so 'https://Admin.RepWorth.net' and a trailing slash still match. The comparison has exactly one owner, isSelfOrigin/normalizeOrigin, shared with assertSameOrigin.

Allowlist parsing: split on ',', trim, drop empty entries (so whitespace and trailing commas are tolerated). An entry containing '*' throws. An entry that is not a parseable absolute URL also throws — loud, and the blast radius is /api/admin/** only, which is what the variable configures. Only a bare trailing slash is accepted (it normalizes away); a non-root path, a query, a fragment or userinfo is REJECTED, not normalized away — discarding them would widen an apparently URL-scoped entry into authority over the whole origin.

An unset or empty ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS admits nothing but loopback (outside production) and this app's own origin. It is NOT an error: that is the correct state of every environment before the Admin app exists.

The loopback rule is exactly http://localhost:<any port> and http://127.0.0.1:<any port>, per ADR 0024 D7's http://localhost:*. https://localhost and http://[::1] are NOT admitted; a dev needing either adds an explicit allowlist entry on a non-production environment.
OPTIONS /api/admin/** with NO Origin header is not a CORS preflight, so it is not short-circuited: it falls through to branch 4 and 401s as it does today.
OPTIONS from this app's OWN origin is answered 204 with the full header set (self is allowed). Harmless — a same-origin fetch never preflights in practice.
The parser is NOT memoized, following src/lib/config/flags.ts: an Edge request parses a one- or two-entry comma list, and memoizing would force a reset dance in tests and prevent a mid-run env stub.

assertSameOrigin keeps its Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site refusal, its missing-Origin refusal and its throw when NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is unset. isSelfOrigin is TOTAL (false on unset/malformed either side), so the proxy never throws from the self-origin test — the allowlist parse is the only throwing path.

When NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is unset, isSelfOrigin returns false, so a Legacy admin portal mutation would be refused 403 origin. That is the same fail-closed direction assertSameOrigin already has (it throws), and NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is a CLIENT_REQUIRED_VARS entry asserted at prebuild — it cannot be unset on a deployed environment.

Allowlist validation is UNCONDITIONAL inside the admin-path boundary and happens BEFORE the self-origin, loopback and missing-Origin shortcuts, so a misconfigured ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS fails loudly on every /api/admin/** request rather than only on the ones that reach the list. It is NOT read on a non-admin request, so a bad value can never break /admin/login or a public page.

A loopback origin is decided by the code rule ALONE: allowed outside the production lane, refused inside it, EVEN IF it is listed in ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS. ADR 0026 D2 says loopback is 'a separate code rule, not a list entry'; letting a listed http://localhost entry win in production would make the production lane's inertness bypassable by configuration.

Parser validation beyond the mandated wildcard throw: an entry must parse as an absolute URL, its scheme must be http: or https:, and it must carry no userinfo, non-root path, query or fragment. new URL() otherwise accepts file:/data: (origin 'null') and rewrites blob:https://admin.example/id to https://admin.example — silently granting an embedded origin. A bare trailing slash is the ONLY non-origin component accepted; it normalizes away.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoes the NORMALIZED origin (new URL(origin).origin), never the raw header. The value written is the canonical serialization of the origin that was matched, not the bytes the caller sent: WHATWG URL parsing strips tabs and newlines, so a raw header can normalize onto an allowlisted origin while differing from it byte for byte. This is a canonical-output argument, not a CR/LF-injection one — plan round 2 measured the installed NextRequest/NextResponse and both throw TypeError on a CR or LF in a header value. For any real browser the raw and normalized forms are identical, so no legitimate caller is affected.

A request Origin that is empty, the literal string 'null' (an opaque origin from a sandboxed iframe or a redirected cross-origin POST), malformed, or multi-valued is REFUSED 403 origin — never treated as absent, and never allowed to throw out of the predicate. Only the allowlist parse throws; the request-side predicate is total.

Vary is MERGED, not overwritten: response.headers.set('Vary','Origin') would discard an existing value such as Accept-Encoding. The stamp appends the Origin token when absent, leaves a '*' value alone, and never duplicates the token.

The proxy reaches the shared own-origin predicate THROUGH src/lib/config/admin-origins.ts rather than importing csrf.ts directly. ADR 0026 D4's requirement is that ONE predicate owns the comparison and no second copy exists; the decision module is the seam ticket item 2 asks for, and a structural test pins that neither src/proxy.ts nor admin-origins.ts spells a second NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL comparison.

assertSameOrigin must NOT inherit the Admin origin allowlist. It keeps refusing an allowlisted Admin app origin and a loopback origin; only isSelfOrigin is shared. Pinned by a test, because reusing the broader admin decision inside CSRF would silently exempt every allowlisted origin from CSRF.

src/proxy.ts is outside every ESLint invariant #1 zone (eslint.config.mjs covers src/app/**, src/instrumentation.ts and src/components/**), so Edge safety is pinned by a source-scan test over the CORS import graph, following the src/lib/auth/__tests__/admin-transport.test.ts 'Edge safety' precedent from #1183.

ci:env-registry enforces the second registry row (.claude/reference/env-vars.md) only for readFlag call sites (scripts/ci/env-registry-audit.ts:756). ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS is a raw process.env read, so only the docs/eservices-variables.md row is machine-enforced; the env-vars.md row is added deliberately because the ticket requires it, and is verified by reading, not by the audit.

Two of the promised tests are characterization, GREEN from the first commit: 'writes no Access-Control header on a non-admin route' and 'assertSameOrigin keeps its four refusals after adopting the shared predicate'. The eval task records them as baseline-green rather than claiming an all-red suite; a collection error is never counted as a red test.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/config/flags.ts — the Edge-safe, un-memoized, single-sanctioned-env-reader house style src/proxy.ts already imports (via src/lib/auth/flags.ts), and the documented one home for VERCEL_TARGET_ENV resolution.
src/lib/auth/admin-transport.ts (#1183) — the precedent for a tiny Edge-safe predicate module that src/proxy.ts and a second consumer both import so the two cannot disagree.
src/lib/shared/csrf.ts assertSameOrigin — the existing URL(x).origin comparison this ticket promotes to a shared predicate rather than re-spelling.
src/lib/shared/protected-routes.ts — the '=== /api/admin || startsWith(/api/admin/)' path-match shape and the normalizePath() casing/trailing-slash discipline.
src/__tests__/proxy.test.ts — the vi.hoisted + vi.mock('@supabase/ssr') harness and the `request(url)` helper; the CORS suite extends it with an origin/method-aware request builder.
src/lib/config/__tests__/flags.test.ts — the process.env stub/delete style for a runtime env reader test.
test_seams: proxy(request) (src/proxy.ts) — the whole contract is asserted on status, JSON body, headers and whether createServerClient was constructed.
readAdminAppOrigins() (src/lib/config/admin-origins.ts) — the env read plus the comma-list parser, driven by process.env.ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS stubs; the parser itself stays internal.
isAllowedAdminOrigin(origin, allowlist) (src/lib/config/admin-origins.ts) — the composed self / loopback / allowlist rule, pure in its second argument.
normalizeOrigin(origin) (src/lib/config/admin-origins.ts) — the canonical origin the proxy echoes in Access-Control-Allow-Origin; null for anything that is not an http(s) origin.
isSelfOrigin(origin) (src/lib/shared/csrf.ts) — the shared own-origin predicate, plus the unchanged assertSameOrigin(request) behaviour above it.
isProductionEnvironment() (src/lib/config/flags.ts) — the lane predicate that makes the loopback rule inert.

rollback_plan: Single PR, no migration and no flag. Revert the merge commit on main and redeploy: /api/admin/** returns to writing no Access-Control-* header, every cross-origin call fails at the browser again, and same-origin Legacy admin portal traffic is unaffected because the self-origin allowance only ever widened what passed. ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS becomes an unread variable and can be left set. On staging, reset staging to origin/main per deployment-guide.md § Re-sync staging. Narrower rollback that does not revert code: clear ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS in the Vercel environment AND REDEPLOY that environment (a running deployment keeps the value it was built with — clearing the variable alone changes nothing), then verify the former origin is refused 403. The allowlist then admits nothing but loopback and this app's own origin, so the Admin app is cut off while the Legacy admin portal keeps working.
observability: A refused origin is greppable in Vercel logs by status alone: 403 on an /api/admin/** path with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin on the response (ADR 0026 D3's stated reason for 403 over a bare 204).
A preflight is distinguishable in Vercel logs as OPTIONS /api/admin/** with a 204 or 403 status; the api-options-volumetric-log WAF rule (#1187, already live) records the volume.

Silent-failure signal to watch after the staging ride: a spike of 403s on /api/admin/** from the app's OWN origin would mean the self-origin allowance broke and the Legacy admin portal's mutations are dead — the ticket's named trap.
No new log line and no token, header value or origin is written to the application logger.
